page_title: tern: a fast, native SSH client

summary.name: tern
summary.one_liner: tern is a fast, native open-source SSH client that connects to saved hosts with a keyboard shortcut and syncs your setup, encrypted, to a Git repo you own.
use_cases: connect quickly to many servers from a keyboard shortcut
manage saved SSH hosts with groups and tags
transfer files over SFTP with drag and drop
sync SSH host and terminal settings across machines
keep low memory use compared with browser-based terminals
summary.what_it_does: tern is a native SSH client that lets you press ⌘K, type a few letters, and connect to a saved host, with hosts ordered by most recent use. Groups, tags, ProxyJump and port forwards are configured per host, and dropped connections reconnect automatically. Logins can come from an SSH key, a password manager command, or tern's encrypted vault, and at a sudo prompt tern types the password when the user presses ⌘\. It includes split panes, find in scrollback, an SFTP panel, snippets, broadcast input to chosen tabs, and session logs. Hosts, snippets and settings can sync to a private Git repository, encrypted with a vault passphrase before leaving the computer.
notable: Native single process with no browser engine; page reports 76 MB vs 580 MB for Tabby on the same server connection
Sudo password is typed only on request via a shortcut, never automatically
Git-based sync encrypted with vault passphrase, with no account or subscription
Customizable wallpaper-driven window colours and 725 terminal themes
caveats: Windows and Linux builds are previews that pass CI but have not yet been run on a real desktop
Signed and notarised builds are listed only for Apple silicon Macs
